searchText: EthStaker + others will host viewing calls: https://www.reddit.com/r/ethstaker/comments/v4631j/ethereum_merge_community_call_series/ https://discord.gg/AFKXHsBv?event=983247689896562709 https://blog.ethereum.org/2022/06/03/ropsten-merge-ttd/ It's not deprecated and is still in the spec. Probably tests doesn't have it because not all clients would respond `ACCEPTED` in those test scenarios ```Payload validation process consists of validating a payload with respect to the block header and execution environment rule sets. ``` little clarification here, does this mean that payload validation do not include execution checks or state root checks? If hashrate on Ropsten doesn't go up, is there a plan to change TTD again? It does include them, the EE rule set denotes a huge part of YP + changes to the execution environment introduced by all hardforks No, we're expecting EF to increase the hashrate and make the Merge transition happen on June 8th as it is planned Ah ok, that makes sense gm frens. I am working on disconnecting from the PoW after ttd. What disconnect reason are clients using when receiving a p2p status message that contains a total difficulty > the terminal PoW block? Right now was gonna use USELESS_PEER but that seems...... rude I feel like subprotocol error is the way to go, but those tend to be vague, and unhelpful to peers Thank you, <@97774605351010304> <@365300888354422794> , will be there! 🐼 Has Ropsten’s hash rate spiked ? Not sure if it’s just devs/EF or not Ah nvm it seems to have gone up but it isn’t massive Yep, we're doing a couple tests to make sure we can make it spike a bit later this week 🙂 I have a quick q regarding the chosen TTD for ropsten (50000000000000000). This is 3.5x the current difficulty of mainnet (just under ~15000000000000000), is it not? Is there by chance a few 0's too many? I see this morning, the difficulty spiked to just under 100 billion, which is equiv to some ~200 3070 GPUs worth of hash power. To get to the chosen TTD, does the calculation not scale linearly? Which would mean we need 100 million 3070s worth of hashpower? or does difficulty not grow linearly to applied hashrate? its the total difficulty, in other words, the cumulative difficulty of all blocks mined to date ahh thanks so much for clarifying - i never understood how basing merge on difficulty would even work if we assume hashrate could heavily stall leading into the merge do you know the geth call to make to get total difficulty? i can look it up nevermind, found it: ``` > eth.getBlock(12336171).totalDifficulty 44348765445734085 ``` thanks again! Kinda wild that the entire Ropsten chain doesn’t have 4 blocks worth of mainnet difficulty 😮 haha so true 🤣 ropsten back down to 3 sec average block time i see 🙂

excerpts.author: stevencook
excerpts.content: I have a quick q regarding the chosen TTD for ropsten (50000000000000000). This is 3.5x the current difficulty of mainnet (just under ~15000000000000000), is it not? Is there by chance a few 0's too many? I see this morning, the difficulty spiked to just under 100 billion, which is equiv to some ~200 3070 GPUs worth of hash power. To get to the chosen TTD, does the calculation not scale linearly? Which would mean we need 100 million 3070s worth of hashpower?

excerpts.author: stevencook
